response.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT rfistat, AVG(modindex) AS avg_modindex FROM signals GROUP BY rfistat), b AS (SELECT AVG(modindex) AS baseline FROM signals), k AS (SELECT g.rfistat, g.avg_modindex, b.baseline FROM g CROSS JOIN b WHERE g.avg_modindex > b.baseline) SELECT rfistat, avg_modindex, avg_modindex - baseline AS above_baseline, avg_modindex - AVG(avg_modindex) OVER () AS diff_from_kept_mean FROM k;

assumptions.assumption: Signals with no RFI status are those where rfistat IS NULL; GROUP BY puts them in one group, shown with a NULL status. Empty-string statuses, if any, stay as their own group.
The baseline is AVG(modindex) over all rows in signals, so each signal counts once and NULL modindex values are ignored.
A group whose modindex values are all NULL has a NULL average, so it is not above the baseline and is dropped.
The 'mean of the kept statuses' averages' is the unweighted mean of the kept groups' averages, with each status counting equally regardless of its signal count.
